    const again = h.assigns(released).find((x) => x.taskId === a.taskId);
    if (!again) throw new Error("no reassignment");
    expect(again).toMatchObject({ connId: "c2", taskId: a.taskId, attempt: 2 });

  }
}

/** The session function's answer is one of three shapes; anything else is a failure. */
export function classifySession(body: string): "live" | "starting" | "off" | "bad" {
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(body) as Record<string, unknown>;
    if (parsed.state === "off" || parsed.kind === "off") return "off";
    if (parsed.state === "starting" || parsed.kind === "starting") return "starting";
    if (typeof parsed.endpoint === "string" && typeof parsed.token === "string") return "live";
    return "bad";
  } catch {
    return "bad";
  }
}

export const handler = async (): Promise<Record<string, number>> => {
  const page = await check(`${webOrigin.replace(/\\/$/, "")}/config.json`);
  const session = await check(sessionUrl);
  const kind = session.ok ? classifySession(session.body) : "bad";
  const metrics = {
    PageOk: page.ok ? 1 : 0,
    SessionOk: kind === "bad" ? 0 : 1,
    Starting: kind === "starting" ? 1 : 0,
  };
  await cloudwatch.send(
    new PutMetricDataCommand({
      Namespace: "Tabframe/Canary",
      MetricData: Object.entries(metrics).map(([MetricName, Value]) => ({
        MetricName,
        Value,
        Unit: "Count",
      })),
    }),
  );
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: "canary", ...metrics, session: kind }));
  return metrics;
};
''')
print("infra/tooling edits ok")

     for (let retry = 0; retry < 3 && !launched; retry++) {
       const candidate = await runWithBackoff({ ..., clientToken: `tabframe-cp-g${generation}-${hour}${retry ? `-r${retry}` : ""}` });
       if (candidate.state === "TERMINATED" || candidate.state === "TERMINATING") { log.warn(...); continue; }
       launched = candidate;
     }
     if (!launched) return null;
     const ready = await waitUntilRunning(launched.microvmId);
     if (!ready) await terminateQuietly(launched.microvmId, "never reached RUNNING");

    new events.Rule(this, "CanaryEvery5", {

      targets: [new targets.LambdaFunction(canary)],

    const canaryMetric = (name: string) =>

      });
    for (const [id, name, description] of [

    ] as const) {
      const alarm = new cloudwatch.Alarm(this, id, {
        alarmDescription: description,
        metric: canaryMetric(name),
        threshold: 1,
        evaluationPeriods: 3,
        datapointsToAlarm: 2,
        comparisonOperator: cloudwatch.ComparisonOperator.LESS_THAN_THRESHOLD,
        treatMissingData: cloudwatch.TreatMissingData.BREACHING,

      evaluationPeriods: 3,

    });

  /** Upload many blobs with one presign round trip; blobs the store already has are skipped. */
  async putMany(blobs: Uint8Array[]): Promise<Array<{ hash: string; size: number }>> {
    const items = await Promise.all(
      blobs.map(async (b) => ({ hash: await sha256Hex(b), size: b.length, bytes: b })),
    );
    const unique = new Map<string, { hash: string; size: number; bytes: Uint8Array }>();
    for (const it of items) unique.set(it.hash, it);
    const presigned = await this.requester.presign(
      [...unique.values()].map(({ hash, size }) => ({ hash, size })),
    );
    const byHash = new Map(presigned.map((p) => [p.hash, p]));
    await Promise.all(
      [...unique.values()].map(async (it) => {
        const p = byHash.get(it.hash);
        if (!p) throw new Error(`no presign for ${it.hash}`);
        if (p.url === null) return;
        // A transient failure is retried a few times (WP8.1): one S3 SlowDown must not end up as a
        // program fault that fails everybody's frame.
        const res = await this.withRetries(() =>
          this.fetchImpl(p.url as string, {

    const urls = Array.from({ length: LIMITS.maxPresignItems }, (_, i) => ({

cd /home/mircea/homework/tabframe; cat > packages/fleet/src/lambda/canary.ts <<'EOF'
// The canary (WP8.2): every five minutes, does the page answer and does the session function say
// something well-formed? It records three metrics — PageOk, SessionOk, Starting — and never touches
// the MicroVM endpoint, which would count as traffic and keep a suspended machine awake.
import { CloudWatchClient, PutMetricDataCommand } from "@aws-sdk/client-cloudwatch";

const cloudwatch = new CloudWatchClient({});
const webOrigin = process.env.TABFRAME_WEB_ORIGIN ?? "";
const sessionUrl = process.env.TABFRAME_SESSION_URL ?? "";

async function check(url: string, ms = 5_000): Promise<{ ok: boolean; body: string }> {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), ms);
  try {
    const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, cache: "no-store" });
    return { ok: res.ok, body: await res.text() };
  } catch {
    return { ok: false, body: "" };
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

/** The session function's answer is one of three shapes; anything else is a failure. */
export function classifySession(body: string): "live" | "starting" | "off" | "bad" {
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(body) as Record<string, unknown>;
    if (parsed.state === "off" || parsed.kind === "off") return "off";
    if (parsed.state === "starting" || parsed.kind === "starting") return "starting";
    if (typeof parsed.endpoint === "string" && typeof parsed.token === "string") return "live";
    return "bad";
  } catch {
    return "bad";
  }
}

export const handler = async (): Promise<Record<string, number>> => {
  const page = await check(`${webOrigin.replace(/\/$/, "")}/config.json`);
  const session = await check(sessionUrl);
  const kind = session.ok ? classifySession(session.body) : "bad";
  const metrics = {
    PageOk: page.ok ? 1 : 0,
    SessionOk: kind === "bad" ? 0 : 1,
    Starting: kind === "starting" ? 1 : 0,
  };
  await cloudwatch.send(
    new PutMetricDataCommand({
      Namespace: "Tabframe/Canary",
      MetricData: Object.entries(metrics).map(([MetricName, Value]) => ({
        MetricName,
        Value,
        Unit: "Count",
      })),
    }),
  );
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: "canary", ...metrics, session: kind }));
  return metrics;
};
EOF

## Everyday

| Task | Command | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Is the machine up? | `mise run health` (`-- --cores` asks each cloud core too) | `/health` and `/diag` of the active control plane through the proxy on the private port, masked. Counts, phase, fleet, snapshotter status, a store round trip, memory. |
| Bring it up | `mise run up` | Sets the pointer to *on*, enables the hourly rule, invokes rotate once. Idempotent: a running control plane is rotated, not duplicated. |
| Take it down | `mise run down` | Disables the rule, terminates every MicroVM from our image, writes *off*. The page shows an off screen; the session function heals nothing. **Destructive: every MicroVM is terminated and the page goes dark until `up`.** |
| Deploy | `mise run deploy` | Builds programs, page, and image; runs lint and every test; `cdk deploy --all`; then `up`, which rotates the running control plane onto the new image. A deploy is a rotation. |
| Rotate by hand | `mise run rotate` | One rotation now (same code the hourly rule runs). |
| Watch logs | `mise run logs`, `mise run logs:fleet` | The MicroVM log group (one stream per VM) and the two functions' groups. See *Observability* for what actually lands. |
| Verify | `mise run verify:m1` / `verify:m2` / `verify:m3` | The milestone runbooks against the live machine: a frame through a kill-half, the editor and word count, a rotation under load. Each prints one line per check and exits non-zero on a failure. |
| Simulate | `mise run sim -- --seed N` | The churn simulation, locally; `--long` for the nightly shape. |

## Cost and budget

- The budget `tabframe-monthly` is $100 with notifications at 50, 80 and 100 % to the address in
  `.env.local`; it never acts on its own (D20 — no automatic kill switch). `tabframe-alarm-test`
  is a one-cent budget created to prove the notification path; delete it once the email has
  arrived: `aws budgets delete-budget --account-id <id> --budget-name tabframe-alarm-test`.
- What costs money while the machine is up: the control plane MicroVM (always, until `down`), two
  cores while anyone is watching, snapshot writes every five seconds while the ledger changes,
  CloudFront and S3 for the page and blobs. Idle, it is one suspended MicroVM's snapshot storage.

--- README 24-45

Three programs ship with the machine and go through the same path as anything you write in the
in-page editor: a distributed **Mandelbrot** render (640 tiles of 64×64 per frame, presets that
advance while anyone watches) and a three-stage **word count** over *Moby-Dick* (map by byte range,
reduce by partition, merge to a top-25). You can also compile your own: the editor holds the
Mandelbrot source and the AssemblyScript compiler runs in a browser worker.

Since M6 a third program ships with the image: **tiny GPT**, an 822 k-parameter character-level
transformer trained on that same corpus, whose whole forward pass runs in WebAssembly on the cores —
one continuation per task, four milliseconds a token, the same bytes on every core
(`docs/feasibility-transformer.md`).

## Why it looks the way it does

Three constraints carry the whole fault-tolerance story; everything else follows from them.

1. **Tasks are idempotent and delivered at least once.** A task may run on two cores, be killed
   halfway, or be handed to a third after its holder vanishes. The program never knows.
2. **Results are single-assignment, memoized by hash.** The first accepted result for a task is
   final; a duplicate is compared, not repeated. With the redundancy toggle on, two cores must
   agree byte for byte before a tile counts, and a disagreement recomputes from scratch and is
   settled by majority after two contested rounds.

Two deploys (generations 99 and 105) each passed three unattended demo passes; the walkthrough found and fixed a core bug (a trapped task's snapshot could not be decoded by a fresh dashboard). --- rationale 126-134

The assignment grades scoping against an eight-hour ceiling and asks for the time spent. This
build went well past that ceiling by deliberate choice: an evening of brainstorming, a day of
design walkthrough (the decisions D1–D20 and the design record), and then the build itself — M0
to M7 across one long session from the evening of 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-04, every milestone
verified against AWS. I kept a time log with two columns because the honest number has two parts.
`docs/timelog.md` records **about 45 hours** of session time in total (measured from the transcripts;
the build session is still open as this is written and the log is finalised with it), plus eight and a
half hours of worker sessions that ran in parallel, of which **<<developer hours>>** were my own hours

// Shared wiring for the operator scripts (run by `mise run rotate|up|down` after the whoami guard).
import { CloudFormationClient, DescribeStacksCommand } from "@aws-sdk/client-cloudformation";
import { EventBridgeRuleControl, LambdaInvoker, SsmPointerStore } from "../src/aws.ts";
import { loadOpsConfig } from "../src/config.ts";
import { SdkMicrovmClient } from "../src/microvm-client.ts";
import type { OpsDeps } from "../src/ops.ts";
import { consoleLogger, realSleeper } from "../src/types.ts";

/** The image ARN embeds the account id, so it is never in the repo: read it from the deployed stack. */
async function resolveImageArn(): Promise<void> {
  if (process.env.TABFRAME_IMAGE_ARN) return;
  const cfn = new CloudFormationClient({});
  const r = await cfn.send(new DescribeStacksCommand({ StackName: "TabframeImage" }));
  const out = r.Stacks?.[0]?.Outputs?.find((o) => o.OutputKey === "ImageArn")?.OutputValue;
  if (!out) throw new Error("TabframeImage stack has no ImageArn output; deploy first");
  process.env.TABFRAME_IMAGE_ARN = out;
}

export async function operatorDeps(): Promise<OpsDeps> {
  await resolveImageArn();
  const config = loadOpsConfig(process.env);
  return {
    pointer: new SsmPointerStore(config.pointerParam),
    microvms: new SdkMicrovmClient(),
    invoker: new LambdaInvoker(),
    rules: new EventBridgeRuleControl(),
    sleep: realSleeper,
    log: consoleLogger,
    config,
  };
}

/** Never let an account id or endpoint token reach the terminal unmasked. */
export function mask(text: string): string {
  return text
    .replace(/\b(\d{8})(\d{4})\b/g, (_m, _h: string, tail: string) => `********${tail}`)
    .replace(/"token":"[^"]+"/g, '"token":"<redacted>"');
}

// `mise run rollback -- <imageVersion>` pins the rotate function to an earlier image version and
// rotates onto it; `mise run rollback -- --clear` removes the pin (WP8.2, finding 27 of loop 1).
// The pin is the function's TABFRAME_IMAGE_VERSION, read at every invocation, so it also holds
// for the hourly rotations until it is cleared — a deploy clears it by redeploying the function.
import {
  GetFunctionConfigurationCommand,
  LambdaClient,
  UpdateFunctionConfigurationCommand,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-lambda";
import { mask, operatorDeps } from "./_deps.ts";

const arg = process.argv[2];
if (!arg || (arg !== "--clear" && !/^\d+$/.test(arg))) {
  console.error("usage: rollback.ts <imageVersion> | --clear");
  process.exit(2);
}

const deps = await operatorDeps();
const lambda = new LambdaClient({});
const name = deps.config.rotateFunctionName;
const current = await lambda.send(new GetFunctionConfigurationCommand({ FunctionName: name }));
const variables = { ...(current.Environment?.Variables ?? {}) };
if (arg === "--clear") delete variables.TABFRAME_IMAGE_VERSION;
else variables.TABFRAME_IMAGE_VERSION = arg;
await lambda.send(
  new UpdateFunctionConfigurationCommand({ FunctionName: name, Environment: { Variables: variables } }),
);
// The configuration update is asynchronous; an invoke before it lands would run the old pin.
for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
  const c = await lambda.send(new GetFunctionConfigurationCommand({ FunctionName: name }));
  if (c.LastUpdateStatus === "Successful") break;
  if (c.LastUpdateStatus === "Failed") throw new Error(`rotate function update failed: ${c.LastUpdateStatusReason}`);
  await deps.sleep(1_000);
}
console.log(arg === "--clear" ? "image pin cleared" : `image pinned to version ${arg}`);
const result = await deps.invoker.invokeSync(name, { reason: "operator" });
console.log(mask(JSON.stringify(result)));
EOF

## Findings

1. `[H] rotation / authority — packages/control-plane/src/server.ts:151-160, packages/core/src/apply.ts:155-160, packages/core/src/fleet.ts:79-85 — A successor launched with a snapshotKey becomes phase "active" at /run (adoptLedger), before /adopt and before the pointer names it; a predecessor whose handover is not followed by a drain also returns to "active" after the 90 s lease. Both run fleetTick and both count the same cores. — Rotate (5-minute Lambda, fleet-stack.ts:105) can die between adopt and promote or between promote and drain (readyTimeout 180 s + two fleet calls of up to ~66 s each exceed the budget). Then two active generations fight: each sees the other's cores as "unlinked" and terminates them after CORE_LINK_TIMEOUT_MS, relaunches, and the replacements connect to the other side — a kill/launch cycle every two minutes, for minutes (EventBridge retry repairs a pending successor) or eight hours (a promoted-but-undrained predecessor is never terminated: repair() knows only pending; rotate never lists VMs). The lease made the second case symmetric (loop 1 regression). — Gate fleet, loop, and assignment on being named: the process polls its own sessionUrl (already in the payload) and acts only while session.generation === its generation; boot into a "standby" phase until /adopt or that check passes; on lease expiry self-drain when the session's generation is newer instead of reverting to active; have rotate list(imageArn) and terminate serving control planes that are neither current nor pending. Cover it with a two-process rotation test that kills the fleet between steps.`

2. `[H] result integrity — packages/core/src/results.ts:49-50,137-157 — A result for an attempt the node never held is refused only when it carries an error; a plain result still settles an open task (requiredAgreement 1 accepts it at once, and two sockets from one client satisfy requiredAgreement 2). scheduler.test.ts:313-338 leans on this. — Task ids are sequential and exposed to observers; any visitor with the public token can paint the frame, or settle the plan task with a stage spec of its own and hijack the execution; the "verified duplicate" story is hollow. Loop 1's #19 fix is incomplete. — Settle open tasks only from a known attempt (any outcome, so a thawed node's late result still counts); let unknown attempts verify or contest settled tasks only, as the loop-1 decision text states; adapt the two tests so the late reporter holds an attempt.`

3. `[H] snapshot / unbounded input — packages/core/src/apply.ts:609-621,637-649, packages/protocol/src/fs.ts:29 — programManifest.defaultParams is an unbounded record (only the 64 KB PROGRAM_MANIFEST_CAP applies) and page 0 of every snapshot carries every non-retired program's defaultParams; pagination only splits task rows. — One dropped manifest with ~60 KB of defaultParams makes page 0 exceed LIMITS.maxMessageBytes, so every subscribe closes with "frame too large" and no dashboard can connect until the program is retired — which happens only at the next adopt, only if unreferenced and over an hour old. ledger.programs itself has no cap (6 uploads a minute per observer). — Bound defaultParams like launch params (PARAMS_MAX_BYTES); drop defaultParams from ProgramView or page programs separately; cap unshipped programs (retire the oldest unreferenced beyond, say, 64 at addProgram); assert page 0 fits before sending and degrade (omit programs) rather than close.`

4. `[M] store effects — packages/control-plane/src/server.ts:328-331, packages/core/src/executions.ts:350,228 — A fetchBlob that throws (S3 5xx/throttle after the SDK's retries, BlobTooLarge) is dispatched as blobFetched bytes: null, which onStageSpec treats as "stage spec blob missing" (execution failed) and onInheritRoot as "expired-root" (a persist program restarts from the bundle). — Loop 1's resumePending retry never runs because the error is delivered as a definitive answer; one transient store error kills the frame or silently discards a persist lineage. The sim never fails a store effect, so it cannot see this. — Distinguish not-found from error in the event ({bytes: null, reason: "missing" | "error"}); on error leave waitingSince set so the STORE_RETRY_MS re-derivation retries; fail only on a confirmed 404 (or after N retries) and name BlobTooLarge in the failure.`

5. `[M] core identity — packages/core/src/apply.ts:506-513, packages/core/src/ledger.ts:371-383, packages/control-plane/src/cores.ts:249-256 — A core is linked by a self-declared hostId, NodeView publishes hostId to every observer, and a hello with an unknown core-microvm-* id creates a CoreRecord. — Any visitor can read a real core's id, hello with it (the record relinks to the impostor), disconnect, and two minutes later fleetTick terminates the live core — repeatable, bypassing the control cooldown. A bogus id makes cores.size satisfy DESIRED_CORES (no real core is launched) and makes gone() throw on GetMicrovm, blinding the reaper while it exists. Deferred #36, now concrete. — Put a per-core secret in the run payload (e.g. HMAC(fleetSecret, microvmId)) and require it in hello; never create or relink a record from hello alone; remove hostId from NodeView; try/catch per id in gone().`

6. `[M] presign budget — packages/core/src/apply.ts:261,267-273 — PRESIGN_BYTES_PER_CONN is a lifetime cap per connection, charged before the store answers and again for blobs already present. — An honest core or tab rendering Mandelbrot (640 × 16 KB per frame) reaches 1 GiB within roughly an hour and is closed as "rate limited", releasing its work and rejoining as a new node — periodic churn and misleading logs — while a hostile client simply reconnects, so the bound protects nothing (loop 1 regression). — Make it a refilling byte bucket (e.g. 64 MB/min per connection) or exempt presigns whose sizes fit the tasks the node holds.`

7. `[M] snapshot lineage — packages/control-plane/src/server.ts:274-280,533-536,604-614, packages/control-plane/src/snapshotter.ts:46-47, packages/fleet/src/lambda/rotate.ts:400-411 — The snapshotter writes latest.json.gz whenever role is control-plane, including while handing-over and after drain; the terminate hook forces a write, so every rotation leaves latest pointing at the predecessor's drained ledger until the successor next changes. latestSnapshotKey() always returns that one key, and /adopt's repeat guard compares meta.seq, which only advances with observers and says nothing about lineage. — A heal or the next launch boots from a stale lineage, and a successor that booted from a higher-seq stale snapshot then refuses the real handover as a "repeat". — Write latest only while active; key snapshots so the fleet picks the highest generation not below the pointer's; replace the seq comparison with "this control plane already adopted a handover" (a flag), otherwise take the handover.`

8. `[M] rotate idempotency and time budget — packages/fleet/src/rotate.ts:131,138-145, packages/fleet/src/config.ts:363-364, packages/fleet/src/cp-client.ts:149,192 — The client token is g${generation}-${hour}; after repair() terminates a stale pending successor, launch() in the same hour relaunches the same generation with the same token and resolves to the terminated VM → "did not reach RUNNING" → failed until the hour turns. The step timeouts (180 s ready, up to ~66 s each for handover and adopt, drain, grace) exceed the function's 5 minutes. — Loop 1's #26 fix is incomplete and the timeout mismatch is the trigger for finding 1. — Use generation plus a fresh nonce in the token (pending already deduplicates); raise the function timeout to 10 minutes or cut readyTimeoutMs to 90 s and cap the fleet calls' total.`

9. `[L] inheritance — packages/core/src/executions.ts:148-164,557,814-849 — inherit resolves by execution id against a ledger that keeps only 32 ended executions. — The loop finishes a Mandelbrot frame every few seconds, so a persist program's latest run is evicted within minutes; a later launch starts empty with no message (only an explicit id says "nothing to inherit"). Deferred #37, concrete. — Keep a bundle → last done root map on the ledger that survives pruning, and inherit by root hash.`

10. `[L] endpoint capacity — packages/control-plane/src/server.ts:394, design §9.7 — The control plane accepts upgrades until the endpoint's 16-connection quota is exhausted, including by clients. — With fifteen tabs open every /handover and /drain gets 429, each rotation degrades to a snapshot handover and the predecessor is terminated with clients undrained. — Refuse the upgrade with 503 when conns.size ≥ 14, keeping two connections for the fleet; say so in §9.7.`

11. `[L] handover clock and state — packages/control-plane/src/server.ts:581, packages/core/src/handover.ts:152-159 — beginHandover defaults now to Date.now() while tick uses clock.now(), and it moves a drained control plane back to handing-over (then, via the lease, to active). — The lease is untestable with an injected clock end to end, and a misdirected /handover resurrects a drained generation. — Pass clock.now(); refuse handover when phase is drained.`

## Summary

The core is in good shape: the ledger invariants, the re-derived store effects, the evidence rules, the cooldown, the solicited bucket, and the redundancy-off settlement all hold up under reading and the churn simulation passes — but the simulation drives one ledger with a store that never fails, so everything that went wrong in this loop lives at the seams the sim cannot reach: two live generations, the fleet's clock budget, the process's error-to-event translation, and what a hostile socket may claim. Fix first the authority gap (a control plane must act only while the session URL names its generation, and boot in standby), second the result-integrity hole (only a held attempt settles an open task), and third the snapshot's unbounded page 0 (bound `defaultParams`, cap programs, degrade instead of closing). After those, the store-error semantics (finding 4) and the presign lifetime cap (finding 6) are small changes that remove two ways an honest machine wedges or churns on its own.

## Findings

1. `[H] core identity / fleet — packages/core/src/apply.ts:506-513, packages/core/src/executions.ts:775-781, packages/core/src/fleet.ts:79-85, packages/infra/lib/image-stack.ts:81-91 — onHello links or creates a CoreRecord from the client-chosen hostId (core-microvm-<id>, kind core); cloud-core ids are public in every snapshot (nodeView.hostId, ledger.ts:371-383), and if the vended endpoint hostname embeds the MicroVM id as fleet/src/testing/fake.ts:115 models, so is the control plane's own. A kill-half that picks the impostor, or just disconnecting and waiting CORE_LINK_TIMEOUT (2 min), makes the control plane call TerminateMicrovm on that id; fake records also count toward DESIRED_CORES (fleet.ts:90-97) and cost a GetMicrovm each per 30 s — any anonymous visitor can kill the cloud cores (possibly the control plane) repeatedly, starve the fleet, and churn RunMicrovm; this is the deferred core-identity item made concrete — never create a record in onHello, link only an existing unlinked record, add a random per-core token to the core run payload (cores.ts:31-40) and a coreToken field in hello and link only on match, replace hostId in nodeView with an opaque label.`

2. `[H] sandbox / scheduler — packages/core/src/results.ts:57-62 (RELEASED returns before compute accounting at :75, no attempt cap), packages/node/src/tasks.ts:91-94 and :191-198 — a program that spins (deadline) or aborts with text matching the hostFailure regex ("out of memory", "HTTP 500", "network error"…) is reported RELEASED by every node, re-queued at the front, never fails, never charges computeMsUsed; task.attempts grows unbounded (every record rides snapshots and /handover, MAX_LEDGER_BYTES 64 MB) and each cycle broadcasts two events to every observer — one upload (6/min, queue 32) burns every visitor's CPU and both cloud cores indefinitely, the §5.5 compute budget is bypassed, snapshots grow until rotation fails, and only a human pressing skip ends it — charge released attempts their deadline window (deadlineAt − assignedAt) against computeMsUsed, cap attempts per task (e.g. 8) and fail it as a program fault beyond that, and in tasks.ts never classify errors starting with abort:/trap:/link: as host failures.`

3. `[M] presign amplification (loop 1 regression) — packages/core/src/apply.ts:202-208, 224-231; packages/protocol/src/node.ts:63-68; packages/store/src/s3.ts:55-89 — the solicited bucket charges one token per presign message, each message carries 64 items, and each item costs a HeadObject plus getSignedUrl; sizes of 1 byte cost nothing against the byte budget — one node connection can drive ~16 k S3 HEADs and signatures per second, exhausting the 1 GB control plane's CPU (heartbeats stall, nodes declared gone) at roughly $23/hour of S3 requests — charge the bucket per item, allow one outstanding presign per connection (the clients already do), dedupe hashes.`

4. `[M] store write bound (loop 1 regression) — packages/core/src/apply.ts:174-181, 261, 266-273; packages/store/src/s3.ts:63-79 with store.test.ts:117 showing content-length is not a signed header — the 1 GiB budget is per socket (a reconnect refills it) and counts a self-declared size; S3 enforces only the checksum pin, so a presign for "1 byte" accepts a 5 GB object whose key is its own hash — unbounded S3 fill through the public endpoint, kept a year on a RETAIN bucket, against a notification-only budget — add content-length to signableHeaders (S3 then rejects a mismatched length; verify against the real bucket as WP1.10 did), budget per hostId or machine-wide per hour in meta, and tag uploads for a shorter lifecycle than the shipped bundles.`

5. `[M] IAM (loop 1 regression) — packages/infra/lib/fleet-stack.ts:44-52 scopes RunMicrovm to the image only when called with a single-action list, and both call sites (:82, :120-126) pass several, so rotate and session keep anyImageArn; packages/infra/lib/image-stack.ts:81-91 grants the control plane Run/Get/Terminate on any image; packages/infra/test/synth.test.ts:236-247 asserts action names only — loop-1 finding #24 is recorded as fixed but the deployed policy is unchanged, and the control plane (which acts on untrusted input, finding 1) may run or terminate any MicroVM in the account and pass any connector (PassNetworkConnector on *) — a separate statement RunMicrovm → image.imageArn for rotate and the control plane, and a synth assertion on that statement's Resource.`

6. `[M] endpoint quota / per-IP (deferred) — packages/control-plane/src/server.ts:390-412 (onUpgrade sees no client address), packages/core/src/apply.ts:552-563, 592-651 (every subscribe rebuilds and sends the whole snapshot) — one client can hold all 16 endpoint connections (the 256/64 caps never bind), and a connect-subscribe-close loop pulls 100 KB+ per subscribe against the VM's ~2 MB/s egress, starving live observers — cheap anonymous lock-out of the public URL — log req.headers once in onUpgrade to learn whether the proxy forwards x-forwarded-for; if so cap sockets and subscribes per address, if not throttle per requestContext.http.sourceIp in packages/fleet/src/session.ts:106-134 and vend per-client one-minute tokens; memoise pages per meta.seq (saves CPU, not egress).`

Verified as real and complete: size-capped fetches (store/driver.ts, bundles.ts caps), presign size/count bounds, one memory per module (validate.ts:36-40), the solicited bucket, the cooldown, RETAIN buckets, fleet routes closed before the secret arrives, pinned tools, and the CloudFront headers; `bun test` on the loop-1 suites passes 50/50. Transcripts show no account ids, tokens, or emails by the shapes checked.

## Summary

The first loop hardened the byte paths (fetch caps, checksum-pinned uploads, headers) and the process lifecycle, but the public control surface still trusts what a client says about itself: a hello can name a real MicroVM and get it terminated, a RELEASED result is free and endless, and the write and presign bounds count self-declared numbers per socket. Two claimed fixes are not what the doc says — RunMicrovm is still image-wide for every launcher and the presign bound meters messages rather than S3 calls. Fix first: (1) stop linking or creating cores from hostId and add the per-core token, (2) charge released attempts to the compute budget with an attempt cap and stop treating abort text as host failure, (3) scope RunMicrovm and Terminate properly and meter presigns per item with a signed content-length so the store budget is real.

## Summary

The tree is in good shape: the loop-1 fixes I traced (store size caps, presign timeout and HeadObject tolerance, params/queue caps, the cooldown, the one-reload guard, the LRU blob cache, dropped-click reporting on the dashboard, `holdWanted`) are present and the 74 web unit tests pass, but three of them are half-done (the compile-worker reset, drop reporting in the editor tab, the ledger signature) and one introduced a real wedge: the 64-item presign cap against a 256-file write cap plus an unguarded `presigned` frame makes any many-file task loop across the cluster on AWS while passing locally. Fix first the presign chunking and frame guard (1), then the `BlobCache` null re-fetch loop that the demo's `broken` program triggers deterministically (2), then the editor's hung-worker and silent-drop paths (3, 4). The rest are cheap and mostly about the page keeping its promises — Stop shown as stopped, counters that mean what they say, lists that are not rebuilt every frame, and a keyboard that can leave the source box.

## Summary

The fleet is now failure-visible (thrown rotations, alarms, retries) and the deploy is gated and sequential, but the deploy path still has two silent traps — a bare `cdk deploy` publishes the placeholder image and can disable the schedule, and a rotation that dies after the pointer flip leaves two active control planes — and the build stamp the first loop added never reaches the image. Fix first: default the image staging to `image-dist` with a placeholder refusal and a `deploy:stacks` task; make the retire step crash-safe (`retiring` in the pointer plus a self-check at lease expiry) and widen the rotate timeout; ship `build.json` in the Dockerfile. Then land the deferred items as specified above — the `rollback` task with the version carried in the run payload so cores follow the pin, digest and NEVRA pinning with a build-time Node assertion, `cdk diff --security-only --fail` and a CI synth, per-task `.env.local`, and a session-level canary that never wakes the machine.

3. `[M] README l.4–5, index.html footer, host.ts spawn hints, editor-core.ts limits sentence, design §16, walkthrough R6 — "core" still means three things: README "Every worker is a core … your tab is a core", footer "every visitor is a core", hints "lends no cores / lend real cores", limits sentence "given to another core", glossary "Node / core — a tab worker or a MicroVM", while R6 says node = any worker and core = a cloud node — and R6's own example ("this tab lends no cores") breaks R6. — The first sentence a reviewer reads teaches a word the page then uses differently ("9 nodes · 3 hosts", "cloud cores"). — Decide once: either adopt R6 everywhere (README "Every worker is a *node* — a thread in someone's tab, or one of the two MicroVMs, the *cloud cores*"; footer "every visitor is a node"; hints "lends no nodes"; glossary split into Node and Cloud core) or amend R6 to "core = any worker; cloud core = one in a MicroVM; node = the ledger's word for a connected core" and align the pills and hints.`

4. `[M] README l.122, design §9.7 l.499, rationale l.103, m3-verification l.63 — "one control plane serves about fifteen browser tabs" — a plain tab costs two of the 16 connections (its dashboard socket and its node's socket, D3/§3) and the two cloud cores cost two more; wp-4.5 says it right ("a dashboard costs one connection and each node one more … about a dozen nodes"), and the demo is scoped to ten nodes across two dashboards for that reason. — A reviewer who opens eight tabs and sees 429s finds the number wrong in four documents. — "about seven tabs each lending a node (a tab costs two connections, its dashboard and its node; the cloud cores cost two more), or fifteen observe-only tabs".`

5. `[M] docs/implementation/wp-8.1-review-loop-1.md — row 11, row 44–52, the totals — row 11 says "a cooldown of three seconds" but packages/core/src/apply.ts:263 has CONTROL_COOLDOWN_MS = 2_000 and design §17 says two; row 44–52 points at "the diffs to … packages/sdk-as/README.md", but commit 20dd4c8 did not touch that file (last change 2026-09-02; the cut was made in editor-core.ts); the table reconciles to 36 accepted, 9 accepted in part, 6 deferred, 1 rejected-as-a-change, while plan.md says "40 accepted, 11 deferred, 1 rejected" and the index and merge commit say "40 landed". — The note is the evidence the loop was done carefully; a number that contradicts the code, a diff that does not exist, and totals its own table cannot produce undo that. — Write "two seconds"; say where each documentation fix actually landed; add one line under the table with counts derived from it and reuse them in plan.md and docs/implementation/README.md; add a legend for dist / sec / fs / tw / devops.`

6. `[M] wp-8.1-review-loop-1.md — row 44–52 and the end of the table — nine technical-writer findings share one row, one severity "H–L", one verdict; nothing lists what loop 2 owes. — Every other finding has a verdict a reader can check; here the reviewer cannot tell what was found or where it changed, and must scan 43 rows for "Deferred". — Give the nine their own rows (finding → file → change) and close with a "Deferred to loops 2–3" list of the six (22, 23, 27, 28, 36, 42).`

7. `[M] /guide.html (editor-core.ts guideMarkdown) and packages/sdk-as/README.md — the loop-1 cut at "## Compiling" also drops the "Allowed imports" paragraph (tf.stat … env.abort; Date.now, Math.random, WASI rejected at upload; never write NaN) and the memory-maximum note; limitsSentence() does not mention imports. — The guide page promises "what a program may do"; a page author now learns the allowlist from a rejected upload. — Move "Allowed imports" and the NaN caveat above "## Compiling" (a "What a program may do" section); keep the asc command and Tooling below the cut.`

8. `[M] docs/runbook.md — "Everyday › Deploy", "Deploy, step by step", "Observability" — no word of the WP8.1 guard: deploy refuses a dirty tree or a HEAD not on origin/main (packages/infra/scripts/deploy-guard.ts; TABFRAME_DEPLOY_UNGATED=1 skips it), and /health now carries build and imageVersion. — The operator document describes a deploy that no longer works that way; the first deploy from a branch fails with a message the runbook does not explain. — Deploy row: "build → test → guard (clean tree, HEAD on origin/main; TABFRAME_DEPLOY_UNGATED=1 for an emergency deploy from a branch) → cdk deploy --all → up"; add build and imageVersion to step 4 and the /health bullet.`

9. `[M] docs/walkthrough.md — Screen A, "Outdated page" — "reloads itself after 1.5 s … Nothing needed", but since WP8.1 the page reloads once per protocol version and then shows "Reloaded once already: hard-refresh this page (Shift+reload) …" (host.ts 432–443). — The walkthrough is the page's contract and misses a state where the visitor must act. — Add a row: "Outdated, reloaded once | the banner asks for a hard refresh | Shift+reload | a reload loop".`

10. `[L] docs/runbook.md — "What is running", "Cost and budget", "Observability" — "Snapshots … one-day lifecycle" (since WP8.1 scoped to the g prefix; latest.json.gz is kept); "tabframe-alarm-test … delete it once the email has arrived" while plan WP4.7 records it deleted on 2026-09-03; the tabframe-alarms topic appears only in an incident row; "Accepted; see design §9.3 (…)" repeats the sentence before it. — Stale facts and a one-off chore in an operator document. — Fix the lifecycle wording, drop the alarm-test sentence, add a row for the SNS topic and its two alarms, cut the duplicate parenthetical.`

11. `[L] README.md — "Try it, in five clicks", "What it is" — "Spawn 3" is index.html's placeholder; the button reads "spawn N" with N = the browser's threads − 1 (host.ts 183), so most reviewers see "spawn 7"; and "Three programs ship … Mandelbrot … word count … compile your own" is followed by a separate "Since M6 a third program ships" paragraph that reads like a patched count. — First-minute copy that matches neither the screen nor itself. — "spawn N (the larger spawn button, sized to your browser)"; one list of three programs, "Since M6" dropped.`

12. `[L] docs/plan.md "Where we are", docs/rationale.md l.129, docs/design.md §11.2 and §6.7 — the plan still says "M7 closed … Left for Mircea" with WP8.1 checked further down; the rationale says "M0 to M7"; the design's verbatim mise.toml block (tools at latest, a parallel deploy) differs from the file on every line (pinned tools, a sequential guarded deploy) and the WP8.1 drift entry omits the pins; §6.7 says "§6.7 below" from inside §6.7. — Three "where we are" statements are a milestone behind, and a quoted file that does not match invites the question of what else is stale. — Plan: "(2026-09-04, M8 loop 1 merged): loops 2–3 next, then a deploy with three demo passes"; rationale "M0 to M8"; replace the toml block with the task names and "see mise.toml" (or refresh it and note the pins in the drift entry); "(WP6.4, in this section)".`

## Summary

Most of loop one's documentation fixes hold up against the code — the stays-up paragraph matches `skipped-suspended` and the ten/fifteen-minute constants, the 31 Playwright tests and the R1 sentences are exact, every relative link resolves, the §9 order, the rationale's "second extension", the plan's shape and the editor label are right — but two of the twelve rewrites did damage: the drift log now has a garbled sentence and seven entries fused into one 4.4 KB line, and the "first extension" rewrite left a typo in the README's most careful paragraph. The remaining problems are consistency rather than substance: "core" is still defined three ways across README, page, glossary and R6; "fifteen tabs" overstates the connection ceiling by two in four documents; and the loop-one note contradicts the code (three vs two seconds), cites a diff that does not exist, and carries totals its own table cannot produce. Fix first: restore the drift log from commit 9a04588; settle the node/core vocabulary in one place and apply it to README, footer, hints and glossary; make the loop-one note honest (two seconds, real file paths, counts derived from the table, nine doc rows, a deferred list) and carry its numbers into the plan and the index.

export function validateModuleBytes(
  bytes: Uint8Array,
  limits: { memoryPagesMax: number },
): Validation {
  if (bytes.length > LIMITS.maxModuleBytes) {
    return { ok: false, reason: `module is ${bytes.length} bytes, cap ${LIMITS.maxModuleBytes}` };
  }
  if (!WebAssembly.validate(asSource(bytes))) {
    return { ok: false, reason: "not a valid WebAssembly module" };
  }
  // One memory only (WP8.1): with multi-memory a module could declare a small first memory and
  // grow an unbounded second one past the cap the design promises.
  const memories = countMemories(bytes);
  if (memories > 1)

new='''/**
 * The demo's in-page store is bounded (WP8.2): about two frames of tiles, not the whole afternoon.
 * Reads refresh an entry, so the seeded program files and whatever the page keeps showing stay;
 * tiles nobody asks for again are the ones that go.
 */
const DEMO_STORE_CAP = 1500;
class BoundedBlobMap extends Map<string, Uint8Array> {
  override get(key: string): Uint8Array | undefined {
    const v = super.get(key);
    if (v !== undefined) {
      super.delete(key);
      super.set(key, v);
    }
    return v;
  }
  override set(key: string, value: Uint8Array): this {
    super.delete(key);
    super.set(key, value);
    while (this.size > DEMO_STORE_CAP) {
      const oldest = this.keys().next().value;
      if (oldest === undefined) break;
      super.delete(oldest);
    }
    return this;
  }
}
const demoStore = new BoundedBlobMap();

const KINDS = ["function", "table", "memory", "global", "tag"] as const;

/** Read the import (2) and export (7) sections straight from the binary; null when malformed. */
export function readModuleShape(bytes: Uint8Array): ModuleShape | null {
  if (bytes.length < 8) return null;
  if (bytes[0] !== 0x00 || bytes[1] !== 0x61 || bytes[2] !== 0x73 || bytes[3] !== 0x6d) return null;
  let pos = 8;
  const leb = (): number => {
    let result = 0;
    let shift = 0;
    for (;;) {
      const b = bytes[pos++];
      if (b === undefined) throw new RangeError("truncated");
      result |= (b & 0x7f) << shift;
      if ((b & 0x80) === 0) return result >>> 0;
      shift += 7;
      if (shift > 35) throw new RangeError("bad LEB128");
    }
  };
  const name = (): string => {
    const len = leb();
    if (pos + len > bytes.length) throw new RangeError("truncated");
    const text = new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true }).decode(bytes.subarray(pos, pos + len));
    pos += len;
    return text;
  };
  const kindOf = (code: number): string => {
    const k = KINDS[code];
    if (k === undefined) throw new RangeError(`unknown kind ${code}`);
    return k;
  };
  const shape: ModuleShape = { imports: [], exports: [] };
  try {
    while (pos < bytes.length) {
      const id = bytes[pos++];
      const size = leb();
      const end = pos + size;
      if (end > bytes.length) return null;
      if (id === 2) {
        const count = leb();
        for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
          const module = name();
          const field = name();
          const kind = kindOf(bytes[pos++] ?? 255);
          // The descriptor is skipped by kind; only its presence is needed here.
          if (kind === "function") leb();
          else if (kind === "table") {
            pos++;
            const flags = leb();
            leb();
            if (flags & 0x01) leb();
          } else if (kind === "memory") {
            const flags = leb();
            leb();
            if (flags & 0x01) leb();
          } else if (kind === "global") {
            pos += 2;
          } else {
            pos++;
            leb();
          }
          shape.imports.push({ module, name: field, kind });
        }
      } else if (id === 7) {
        const count = leb();
        for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
          const field = name();
          const kind = kindOf(bytes[pos++] ?? 255);
          leb();
          shape.exports.push({ name: field, kind });
        }
      }
      pos = end;
    }
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  return shape;
}

/** The allowlist and the required exports, on a parsed shape. */
export function checkShape(shape: ModuleShape): { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: string } {
  for (const imp of shape.imports) {
    const allowed = ALLOWED_IMPORTS[imp.module];
    if (!allowed?.has(imp.name) || imp.kind !== "function") {
      return { ok: false, reason: `forbidden import ${imp.module}.${imp.name} (${imp.kind})` };
    }
  }
  const exports = new Map(shape.exports.map((e) => [e.name, e.kind]));
  for (const name of REQUIRED_EXPORTS) {
    const kind = exports.get(name);
    const want = name === "memory" ? "memory" : "function";
    if (kind !== want) return { ok: false, reason: `missing export ${name} (${want})` };
  }
  return { ok: true };
}''',1)

  if (opts.compile === false) {
    // The control plane runs no program code (design §2) and compiles none either (WP8.2): the
    // import allowlist and the required exports are read from the binary's own sections, so
    // eight megabytes of a stranger's bytes never reach V8's compiler on the event loop.
    const parsed = readModuleShape(bytes);
    if (!parsed) return { ok: false, reason: "malformed import or export section" };
    const shape = checkShape(parsed);
    if (!shape.ok) return shape;
    return { ok: true, memory, module: null };
  }
  let module: WebAssembly.Module;
  try {
    module = new WebAssembly.Module(asSource(bytes));
  } catch (err) {
    return { ok: false, reason: `compile failed: ${String(err)}` };
  }
  const shape = validateCompiled(module);
  if (!shape.ok) return shape;
  return { ok: true, memory, module };
}

const KINDS = ["function", "table", "memory", "global", "tag"] as const;

/** Read the import (2) and export (7) sections straight from the binary; null when malformed. */
export function readModuleShape(bytes: Uint8Array): ModuleShape | null {
  if (bytes.length < 8) return null;
  if (bytes[0] !== 0x00 || bytes[1] !== 0x61 || bytes[2] !== 0x73 || bytes[3] !== 0x6d) return null;
  let pos = 8;
  const leb = (): number => {
    let result = 0;
    let shift = 0;
    for (;;) {
      const b = bytes[pos++];
      if (b === undefined) throw new RangeError("truncated");
      result |= (b & 0x7f) << shift;
      if ((b & 0x80) === 0) return result >>> 0;
      shift += 7;
      if (shift > 35) throw new RangeError("bad LEB128");
    }
  };
  const name = (): string => {
    const len = leb();
    if (pos + len > bytes.length) throw new RangeError("truncated");
    const text = new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true }).decode(bytes.subarray(pos, pos + len));
    pos += len;
    return text;
  };
  const kindOf = (code: number): string => {
    const k = KINDS[code];
    if (k === undefined) throw new RangeError(`unknown kind ${code}`);
    return k;
  };
  const shape: ModuleShape = { imports: [], exports: [] };
  try {
    while (pos < bytes.length) {
      const id = bytes[pos++];
      const size = leb();
      const end = pos + size;
      if (end > bytes.length) return null;
      if (id === 2) {
        const count = leb();
        for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
          const module = name();
          const field = name();
          const kind = kindOf(bytes[pos++] ?? 255);
          // The descriptor is skipped by kind; only its presence matters here.
          if (kind === "function") leb();
          else if (kind === "table") {
            pos++;
            const flags = leb();
            leb();
            if (flags & 0x01) leb();
          } else if (kind === "memory") {
            const flags = leb();
            leb();
            if (flags & 0x01) leb();
          } else if (kind === "global") {
            pos += 2;
          } else {
            pos++;
            leb();
          }
          shape.imports.push({ module, name: field, kind });
        }
      } else if (id === 7) {
        const count = leb();
        for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
          const field = name();
          const kind = kindOf(bytes[pos++] ?? 255);
          leb();
          shape.exports.push({ name: field, kind });
        }
      }
      pos = end;
    }
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  return shape;
}

/** The allowlist and the required exports, on a parsed shape. */
export function checkShape(shape: ModuleShape): { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: string } {
  for (const imp of shape.imports) {
    const allowed = ALLOWED_IMPORTS[imp.module];
    if (!allowed?.has(imp.name) || imp.kind !== "function") {
      return { ok: false, reason: `forbidden import ${imp.module}.${imp.name} (${imp.kind})` };
    }
  }
  const exports = new Map(shape.exports.map((e) => [e.name, e.kind]));
  for (const name of REQUIRED_EXPORTS) {
    const kind = exports.get(name);
    const want = name === "memory" ? "memory" : "function";
    if (kind !== want) return { ok: false, reason: `missing export ${name} (${want})` };
  }
  return { ok: true };
}

describe("readModuleShape (WP8.2)", () => {
  test("reads the imports and exports from the binary and agrees with the compiled module", async () => {
    const bytes = await compileFixture("echo", { maximumMemory: 256 });
    const shape = readModuleShape(bytes);
    expect(shape).not.toBeNull();
    const compiled = new WebAssembly.Module(bytes as unknown as BufferSource);
    expect(shape?.exports.map((e) => `${e.name}:${e.kind}`).sort()).toEqual(
      WebAssembly.Module.exports(compiled)
        .map((e) => `${e.name}:${e.kind}`)
        .sort(),
    );
    expect(shape?.imports.map((i) => `${i.module}.${i.name}:${i.kind}`).sort()).toEqual(
      WebAssembly.Module.imports(compiled)
        .map((i) => `${i.module}.${i.name}:${i.kind}`)
        .sort(),
    );
    expect(checkShape(shape as NonNullable<typeof shape>).ok).toBe(true);
  });

  test("the no-compile validation names a forbidden import and returns no module", async () => {
    const bytes = await compileFixture("time", { maximumMemory: 256 });
    const v = validateModuleBytes(bytes, limits, { compile: false });
    expect(v.ok).toBe(false);
    if (!v.ok) expect(v.reason).toContain("forbidden import");
    const good = validateModuleBytes(await compileFixture("echo", { maximumMemory: 256 }), limits, {
      compile: false,
    });
    expect(good.ok).toBe(true);
    if (good.ok) expect(good.module).toBeNull();
  });

  test("a truncated import section is malformed, not a crash", () => {
    // magic + version, then an import section claiming ten entries with one byte of payload
    const bytes = new Uint8Array([0, 0x61, 0x73, 0x6d, 1, 0, 0, 0, 2, 1, 10]);
    expect(readModuleShape(bytes)).toBeNull();
    expect(readModuleShape(new Uint8Array([0, 0x61, 0x73, 0x6d, 1, 0, 0, 0]))?.exports).toEqual([]);
  });
});

# Tabframe MicroVM image (design §11.3): one image, two roles, chosen by the run-hook payload.
# The bundle main.js is produced by `mise run build:image`; this directory ships a placeholder
# until then so the image builds and answers its hooks.
# Pinned by digest (WP8.2): two builds of one commit get the same base. Refresh the digest with
# `docker buildx imagetools inspect public.ecr.aws/lambda/microvms:al2023-minimal`.

COPY package.json /app/package.json
COPY main.js /app/main.js

COPY programs/ /app/programs/
# The build stamp (WP8.1, shipped since WP8.2): /health names the commit the image was staged from.
COPY build.json /app/build.json
EXPOSE 8080 8081
CMD ["node", "/app/main.js"]

/**
 * The page's content security policy (WP8.2), one string for CloudFront and the local server, so
 * the browser suites run under the policy the deployed page gets. Scripts come from the page's
 * origin and blob: workers; WebAssembly needs 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; styles are the page's plus inline
 * attributes; nothing frames the page.
 */
export const PAGE_CSP = [
  "default-src 'self' https: wss: data: blob:",
  "script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' blob:",
  "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
  "object-src 'none'",
  "base-uri 'self'",
  "frame-ancestors 'none'",
].join("; ");

/** Locally the sockets and the store are plain http and ws on the loopback. */
export const LOCAL_PAGE_CSP = PAGE_CSP.replace(
  "default-src 'self' https: wss:",
  "default-src 'self' https: wss: http: ws:",
);

/** The stringified Resource of every IAM statement that grants lambda:RunMicrovm. */
function runMicrovmResources(template: Template): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const policy of Object.values(template.findResources("AWS::IAM::Policy"))) {
    const doc = (policy as { Properties?: { PolicyDocument?: { Statement?: unknown[] } } }).Properties
      ?.PolicyDocument?.Statement;
    for (const st of doc ?? []) {
      const actions = JSON.stringify((st as { Action?: unknown }).Action ?? "");
      if (actions.includes("lambda:RunMicrovm"))
        out.push(JSON.stringify((st as { Resource?: unknown }).Resource ?? ""));
    }
  }
  return out;
}

presigns cost one solicited token per item against a refilling 64 MiB-per-minute byte budget, and the schema caps a request at 24 items so a `presigned` frame of signed URLs fits one message (§7.1); the S3 presign signs the content length as well as the checksum; the control plane validates a module's imports and exports from the binary's sections and compiles nothing (§2); rotate records `retiring` in the pointer so a retire a dead run left behind is finished first, retries a client token that resolved to a terminated VM with a `-r<n>` suffix, waits 120 s for RUNNING, and runs with a ten-minute timeout (§9.2); import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { encode, LIMITS } from "@tabframe/protocol";
import { H, harness } from "./harness.ts";

// Loop 2 (WP8.2): page 0 of a snapshot must fit one frame whatever the programs carry.
describe("snapshot page 0 under heavy programs", () => {
  test("sixty-four programs with four kilobytes of defaults each still subscribe, with the defaults stripped", () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.hello("a", "h1");
    const heavy = { blob: "x".repeat(3_900) };
    for (let i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
      const c = (i + 10).toString(36).padStart(2, "0");
      h.event({
        kind: "programAdded",
        bundle: H(c[0] ?? "a").slice(0, 62) + c,
        module: H("d"),
        manifest: { name: `p${i}`, view: "tiles", persist: false, defaultParams: heavy },
        files: {},
      });
    }
    const effects = h.subscribe("obs");
    const pages = effects.filter((e) => e.kind === "send" && e.msg.t === "snapshot");
    expect(pages.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const e of pages) {
      if (e.kind !== "send") continue;
      // encode() throws over the cap; nothing here does.
      expect(new TextEncoder().encode(encode(e.msg)).length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(LIMITS.maxMessageBytes);
    }
    const first = pages[0];
    if (first?.kind === "send" && first.msg.t === "snapshot" && "programs" in first.msg) {
      const programs = first.msg.programs as Array<{ defaultParams: Record<string, unknown> }>;
      expect(programs.length).toBe(64);
      expect(programs.every((p) => Object.keys(p.defaultParams).length === 0)).toBe(true);
    } else {
      throw new Error("page 0 carries the cluster");
    }
    // A light ledger keeps its defaults.
    const light = harness();
    light.hello("a", "h1");
    light.event({
      kind: "programAdded",
      bundle: H("e"),
      module: H("d"),
      manifest: { name: "light", view: "tiles", persist: false, defaultParams: { preset: 1 } },
      files: {},
    });
    const page0 = light.subscribe("obs").find((e) => e.kind === "send" && e.msg.t === "snapshot");
    if (page0?.kind === "send" && page0.msg.t === "snapshot" && "programs" in page0.msg) {
      const programs = page0.msg.programs as Array<{ defaultParams: Record<string, unknown> }>;
      expect(programs.some((p) => p.defaultParams.preset === 1)).toBe(true);
    }
  });
});
EOF

3. `[M] web/host + editor-page — packages/web/src/host.ts:1107-1111, 1160; packages/web/src/editor-page.ts:74-77, 125 — \`fetch("/config.json")\` (and its JSON parse) has no try/catch or retry and \`void main()\` swallows the rejection — a blip on that one request leaves the dashboard on "Connecting… the page keeps trying on its own" (banners.ts:52) for ever, which is false, and the editor tab stuck on its static "connecting to the machine…" text — wrap in a retry loop with backoff and surface the failure in the connection banner.`

## Summary

Fix the observer client first (1, 2): every state the walkthrough promises flows through its reconnect path, and it currently both fires stale destructive controls after a resubscribe and, after a day of hourly rotations, takes up to 30 s to come back — both reproduced with a fake socket, both untested. Then close the two places where a single failed request becomes a permanent lie (3, 5), and re-key the panel rebuilds (4) since they undo loop 2's keyboard work and are the page's largest remaining DOM churn. Items 6–11 are contract polish against docs/walkthrough.md; 12 is hygiene. The unit suite for these packages passes (180 tests, 17 files), `tsc` on packages/web is clean, and biome reports only CSS `!important` warnings. Loop-2 claims I verified as real and complete in the code: rows 3 (`defaultParams` ≤ 4 KB in fs.ts), 12 (`hostFailure` refuses `abort:|trap:|link:`), 13 (`maxPresignItems` = 24 and batched `putMany`), 23 (timeout and death terminate the worker), 24 (`sendStatus`, `onDropped` to `#launchInfo`, "launched" only on the echo — with the name-matching caveat in 7), 25 (`seededFailure`, no `lastFailure` on a stop, and the core does emit `cancelled` + "stopped by a person"), 26 (`BoundedBlobMap` 1500), 27 (Shift+Tab/Escape, `tabindex`/`role` rows), 28 (`OFF_POLL_MS` in both clients), 29–31 (per-seq held count, activity signature and cap 400, verified/mismatched in the ledger signature), plus loop-1 rows 12–14, 16, 39–41; the only claim that does not fully hold is row 22's "version not bumped for a miss" (finding 4).</result>

/** Fetches from `<storeBase>/<hash>` with the cache the CDN allows: blobs are immutable. */
export function storeSource(storeBase: string, fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch): BlobSource {
  const base = storeBase.replace(/\/$/, "");
  return {
    async get(hash) {
      const res = await fetchImpl(`${base}/${hash}`, { cache: "force-cache" });
      if (res.status === 404 || res.status === 403) return null;
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`blob ${res.status}`);
      return new Uint8Array(await res.arrayBuffer());
    },
  };

  private releaseHeld(): void {
    const now = Date.now();
    const fresh = this.held.filter((h) => now - h.at <= CONTROL_HOLD_MS);
    const dropped = this.held.length - fresh.length;
    this.held = [];
    // A click that waited longer than the hold is dropped, and said so (WP8.1, rule R2).
    if (dropped > 0) this.handlers.onDropped?.(dropped);
    for (const h of fresh) {
      if (h.control.t === "setRedundancy") {
        this.state = withRedundancy(this.state, h.control.on);
        this.handlers.onCluster(this.state);
      }
      this.outbox.push(h.control);
    }
    if (fresh.length > 0) this.drain();
  }

  private drain(): void {
    if (this.sendTimer || this.outbox.length === 0) return;
    const wait = this.lastSentAt + CONTROL_SPACING_MS - Date.now();
    if (wait > 0) {
      this.sendTimer = setTimeout(() => {
        this.sendTimer = null;
        this.drain();
      }, wait);
      return;
    }
    const control = this.outbox.shift() as Outgoing;
    const session = this.session;
    if (!this.connected || !session) {
      // The socket went between the click and the send: controls wait for the next subscribe,
      // a presign does not (its upload would have to start over anyway).
      const now = Date.now();

export function storeSource(storeBase: string, fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch): BlobSource {
  const base = storeBase.replace(/\\/$/, "");

 * `immutable` header keeps a 200 for a year, while `force-cache` would have replayed a stored 404
 * for a tile asked for a moment before its upload landed. A 5xx or a network error is retried

export function storeSource(storeBase: string, fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch): BlobSource {

      let lastError: unknown = null;
      for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {

          if (res.status === 404 || res.status === 403) return null;
          if (res.status >= 500) {

/** Clear the off state (keeping the generation) and ask rotate to launch a control plane. */
export async function up(deps: OpsDeps): Promise<unknown> {
  const p = await deps.pointer.read();
  await deps.pointer.write({ ...p, state: "on", updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() });

  deps.log.info("up: pointer set to on, rotation schedule enabled, invoking rotate");
  return deps.invoker.invokeSync(deps.config.rotateFunctionName, { reason: "up" });
}

function onHeartbeat(ledger: Ledger, connId: string, msg: Heartbeat, now: number): Effect[] {
  const node = nodeOf(ledger, connId);
  if (!node) return refuse(ledger, connId, CLOSE.invalidMessage, "heartbeat before hello", now);
  node.lastSeen = now;
  node.visible = msg.visible;
  // Throttled is the one label the node's own evidence decides: its host tab is hidden.
  if (!msg.visible && node.health !== "throttled") {
    node.health = "throttled";
    return broadcast(ledger, { t: "nodeHealth", nodeId: node.nodeId, health: node.health });
  }
  if (msg.visible && node.health === "throttled") {
    node.health = "fast";
    return broadcast(ledger, { t: "nodeHealth", nodeId: node.nodeId, health: node.health });
  }
  return [];
}

function onSubscribe(ledger: Ledger, connId: string, now: number): Effect[] {
  if (ledger.observers.has(connId))
    return refuse(ledger, connId, CLOSE.invalidMessage, "duplicate subscribe", now);
  if (ledger.observers.size >= LIMITS.observerCap)
    return refuse(ledger, connId, CLOSE.observerCap, "observer cap reached", now);
  ledger.observers.set(connId, { connId, subscribedAt: now, lastSeen: now, launchedAt: [] });
  ledger.meta.lastInteractionAt = now;
  const effects = snapshotPages(ledger, connId, now);
  effects.push(...ensureDefaultLoop(ledger, now));
  effects.push(...fill(ledger, now));
  return effects;
}

--- scheduler deadline
import { type Assign, type Health, LIMITS, PROTOCOL_VERSION } from "@tabframe/protocol";
import { toBase64 } from "./bytes.ts";
import type { Effect } from "./events.ts";
import type { ExecutionRecord, Ledger, NodeRecord, TaskRecord } from "./ledger.ts";
import { broadcast } from "./observers.ts";

/** Median of the execution's recent compute samples times the factor, floored (design §6.4). */
export function deadlineMs(ledger: Ledger, exec: ExecutionRecord): number {
  const samples = exec.computeSamples;
  if (samples.length === 0) return ledger.config.deadlineFloorMs;
  const sorted = [...samples].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const median = sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)] ?? 0;
  return Math.max(ledger.config.deadlineFloorMs, Math.round(median * ledger.config.deadlineFactor));
}

export function runningAttempts(task: TaskRecord): number {
  return task.attempts.filter((a) => a.outcome === "running").length;
}

function holds(task: TaskRecord, nodeId: string): boolean {
  return task.attempts.some((a) => a.outcome === "running" && a.nodeId === nodeId);
}

/** Results reported in the current contested round that agree with each other, at most. */
function currentRoundResults(task: TaskRecord): number {
  return task.results.filter((r) => r.round === task.contestedRounds).length;
}

/** How many more attempts this task wants before it can settle. */
export function wanted(task: TaskRecord): number {
  if (task.status === "done" || task.status === "failed") return 0;
  return Math.max(0, task.requiredAgreement - currentRoundResults(task) - runningAttempts(task));
}

/** The node already reported this round: a second attempt there could only agree with itself. */
function answered(task: TaskRecord, nodeId: string): boolean {
  return task.results.some((r) => r.round === task.contestedRounds && r.nodeId === nodeId);
}

/** Results and presigns per second per node (WP8.1); maxInFlight keeps an honest node far below. */
export const SOLICITED_RATE = 256;
/** Presigned bytes a connection may ask for per minute (WP8.2): a refilling bucket, so an honest core rendering all day is never closed and
export const PRESIGN_BYTES_PER_MIN = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
/** Destructive controls are applied at most this often, machine-wide (WP8.1). */
export const CONTROL_COOLDOWN_MS = 2_000;
const DESTRUCTIVE = new Set(["killHalf", "freezeHalf", "throttleHalf", "restart", "stop"]);

/** Charge a presign's bytes against the connection's refilling budget (WP8.2); false when it is spent. */
function chargePresign(conn: ConnState, items: Array<{ size: number }>, now: number): boolean {
  let total = 0;
  for (const it of items) total += it.size;
  const b = conn.presignBytes;
  const perMs = PRESIGN_BYTES_PER_MIN / 60_000;
  b.tokens = Math.min(PRESIGN_BYTES_PER_MIN, b.tokens + (now - b.refilledAt) * perMs);
  b.refilledAt = now;
  if (total > b.tokens) return false;
  b.tokens -= total;
  return true;
}

function refill(b: { tokens: number; refilledAt: number }, perMin: number, now: number): void {

/** A fresh core token (WP8.2): the control plane remembers it and the core's hello shows it. */
export function newCoreToken(): string {
  return randomBytes(16).toString("hex");

  const microvms = client ?? new SdkMicrovmClient();

    async launch(): Promise<{ microvmId: string; token: string }> {

        ingressConnectors: [],

        clientToken: `tabframe-core-g${config.generation}-${Date.now()}-${counter++}`,

 * The page's content security policy (WP8.2, tightened in WP8.3), one function for CloudFront and
 * the local server, so the browser suites run under the policy the deployed page gets. Scripts
 * come from the page's origin and blob: workers; WebAssembly needs 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; styles are

 * nothing frames the page and no form posts anywhere.

export function pageCsp(region: string): string {
  return [
    "default-src 'self'",
    `connect-src 'self' https://*.lambda-url.${region}.on.aws wss://*.lambda-microvm.${region}.on.aws https://*.s3.${region}.amazonaws.com`,

    "worker-src 'self' blob:",
    "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
    "img-src 'self' blob: data:",
    "font-src 'self'",
    "object-src 'none'",
    "frame-src 'none'",
    "form-action 'none'",
    "base-uri 'self'",
    "frame-ancestors 'none'",
  ].join("; ");
}

);

class FakeSocket {
  static OPEN = 1;
  static instances: FakeSocket[] = [];
  readyState = 0;
  sent: string[] = [];
  onopen: ((ev: unknown) => void) | null = null;
  onmessage: ((ev: { data: string }) => void) | null = null;
  onclose: ((ev: { code: number; reason: string }) => void) | null = null;
  readonly url: string;
  readonly protocols: string[] | undefined;
  constructor(url: string, protocols?: string[]) {
    this.url = url;
    this.protocols = protocols;
    FakeSocket.instances.push(this);
  }
  open(): void {
    this.readyState = 1;
    this.onopen?.({});
  }
  deliver(msg: Record<string, unknown>): void {
    this.onmessage?.({ data: JSON.stringify(msg) });
  }
  send(data: string): void {
    this.sent.push(data);
  }
  close(code = 1000, reason = ""): void {
    this.readyState = 3;
    this.onclose?.({ code, reason });
  }
  frames(): Array<{ t: string }> {
    return this.sent.map((s) => JSON.parse(s) as { t: string });
  }
}

// The page's configuration (WP8.3): `/config.json` names the session URL. One failed fetch used to
// leave the dashboard on "Connecting… the page keeps trying on its own" for ever, which was false.
// This keeps trying, with a backoff that tops out at thirty seconds, and says what it is doing.

const FIRST_RETRY_MS = 1_000;
const MAX_RETRY_MS = 30_000;

export interface ConfigLoadDeps {
  fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
  sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;
  /** Told about each failure and the wait before the next try. */
  onRetry?: (attempt: number, delayMs: number, reason: string) => void;
}

/** Resolve the session URL from `/config.json`, retrying until it answers. */
export async function loadSessionUrl(origin: string, deps: ConfigLoadDeps = {}): Promise<string> {
  const fetchImpl = deps.fetchImpl ?? fetch;
  const sleep = deps.sleep ?? ((ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)));
  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      const res = await fetchImpl("/config.json", { cache: "no-store" });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`config.json answered ${res.status}`);
      const config = (await res.json()) as { sessionUrl?: unknown };
      if (typeof config.sessionUrl !== "string" || config.sessionUrl.length === 0)
        throw new Error("config.json names no session URL");
      return new URL(config.sessionUrl, origin).toString();
    } catch (err) {
      const delay = Math.min(MAX_RETRY_MS, FIRST_RETRY_MS * 2 ** (attempt - 1));
      deps.onRetry?.(attempt, delay, err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));
      await sleep(delay);
    }
  }
}
EOF

import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("a failed configuration fetch is retried with a growing wait, and the URL is resolved against the origin", async () => {
  let calls = 0;
  const waits: number[] = [];
  const retries: string[] = [];
  const url = await loadSessionUrl("https://page.example", {
    fetchImpl: (async () => {
      calls++;
      if (calls === 1) throw new TypeError("network down");
      if (calls === 2) return new Response("nope", { status: 503 });

    }) as typeof fetch,
    sleep: async (ms) => {
      waits.push(ms);
    },
    onRetry: (_attempt, _delay, reason) => retries.push(reason),
  });
  expect(url).toBe("https://page.example/session");
  expect(waits).toEqual([1_000, 2_000]);
  expect(retries).toEqual(["network down", "config.json answered 503"]);
});

describe("loop 3 (WP8.3)", () => {
  test("controls queued behind the spacing timer survive a silent resubscribe and go out once", async () => {
    const { client, socket } = await live();
    // Two clicks right after the subscribe: both wait behind the 250 ms spacing.
    expect(client.send({ t: "killHalf" })).toBe(true);
    expect(client.send({ t: "stop" })).toBe(true);
    // A sequence gap before they went out: the client swaps sockets.
    socket.deliver({ t: "controlApplied", ...env, seq: 3, at: 2, op: "resumeAll", nodeIds: [] });
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5));
    await tick();
    await tick();
    const next = FakeSocket.instances[1] as FakeSocket;
    next.open();
    next.deliver(snapshot(4));
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, CONTROL_SPACING_MS * 3 + 20));
    const all = [...socket.frames(), ...next.frames()].map((f) => f.t).filter((t) => t !== "subscribe");
    expect(all.sort()).toEqual(["killHalf", "stop"]);
    client.stop();
  });

  test("a healthy session resets the reconnect backoff", async () => {
    const { client, socket } = await live();
    socket.close(1006, "");
    expect(client.lastDelayMs).toBe(LIMITS.reconnectMinMs);
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, LIMITS.reconnectMinMs + 20));
    await tick();
    await tick();
    const next = FakeSocket.instances[1] as FakeSocket;
    next.open();
    next.deliver(snapshot(2));
    next.close(1006, "");
    // Without the reset this would be the second step of the schedule, up to twice as long.
    expect(client.lastDelayMs).toBe(LIMITS.reconnectMinMs);
    client.stop();
  });

  test("a full machine is a state of its own, retried after the server's ten seconds", async () => {
    const { client, states, socket } = await live();
    socket.close(4008, "machine full: 14 clients; retry in 10 s");
    expect(states.at(-1)).toBe("full");
    expect(client.lastDelayMs).toBe(MACHINE_FULL_RETRY_MS);
    client.stop();
  });
});

84	- 5 (whole): Every task of the running execution rides every snapshot, handover, and adopt uncompressed; a program with a few 4096-task stages makes the ledger tens of megabytes on a 2 MB/s endpoint under a 15 s timeout. — Compacting sealed stages, bounding inline input per execution, and gzipping the handover body are a ledger-shape change with its own tests; today's caps (tasks per stage, inline input, results per task) bound it for the shipped programs; the sim and the deploy carry the shipped programs. Recorded as the first follow-up.
85	- 6 (in part): SSM version-conditional writes are *deferred*.
86	- 7 (in part): Periodic reconciliation against `list(imageArn)` is *deferred*.
87	- 8 (whole): The simulation's node never enforces a deadline or sends `RELEASED`, its store never fails, messages are never duplicated or late, and no handover happens mid-run — so it could not see rows 1, 3, 4, 7, or 9. — The gaps are real; a chaos-phase rotation and a stricter virtual node are the second follow-up. Every fix in this loop carries a unit test instead.
88	- 11 (in part): Assignment-derived allowances, skipping the HeadObject for observers, and tagging uploads for a short lifecycle are *deferred*: blobs the ledger references must not expire, so a tag-based lifecycle needs the ledger's word first.
89	- 12 (in part): Per-instance 429s are *deferred*.
90	- 19 (in part): Rate-limiting pause/resume alternation is *deferred*: pause is one observer's hold and costs nothing machine-wide.
91	- 21 (whole): `nodejs22` is installed unpinned beside a digest-pinned base. — The base image is arm64-only and the build host is amd64: querying the exact NEVRA needs emulation. The digest pins the base; `node --version` in the build log makes drift visible.
92	- 26 (in part): Keying each panel on the hashes it shows is *deferred*.
93	- 31 (in part): Arrow-key selection on the canvases is *deferred*.
94	- 34 (in part): Hoisting the duplicated helpers is *deferred* as hygiene.
95	
96	The two whole deferrals (5 and 8) are the follow-ups for after the loops: compacting sealed stages so the ledger stays small under large programs, and a simulation whose node enforces deadlines and releases, whose store fails, and which rotates mid-run.
97	
98	## Tests
99	
100	- Core: once-per-attempt charging and the ignored replayed release, the doubled deadline and the `lost` outcome, the heartbeat window and the two-second health announcement, the destructive set, the machine-wide presign and launch budgets (tokens in the harness and the simulation), `seq` advancing unobserved; protocol: the canvas cap in the property test and a full `presigned` reply.
101	- Fleet: `retiring` and the pin round-trip through the codec, the early `pending` record, the two-pass `down`, the canary's three bodies, the session memo.
102	- Control plane: the lease self-check with a failed read re-arming, the standby gate (a control plane whose pointer names another launches no cores), the memoised resolution.
103	- Infra: every COPY source exists in the placeholder directory; every AWS-touching task carries the identity and the guard; no RunMicrovm statement names a wildcard image.
104	- Web: kept controls across a resubscribe, the reset backoff, the machine-full state, the bundle-matched launch, the stopped result box; the browser suites pass locally under the region's policy.
105	- Every browser suite passes locally; the CDK app synthesises without credentials (as CI does).
106	
107	## Drift
108	
109	`docs/design.md` §17 entry of 2026-09-04 (WP8.3); §6.4 (deadline growth), §11.3 (the Dockerfile pointer); the README, runbook, walkthrough, rationale, plan, timelog, and both earlier loop notes as listed in row 44.

test("a program that never returns is killed at the deadline and its task is given away", async ({
  page,
}) => {
  test.setTimeout(300_000);
  await page.goto("/");
  await expect(page.locator("#machine")).toHaveText(/live/, { timeout: 30_000 });
  await page.evaluate(watch);
  // Three nodes: the spinner holds one, the others must carry the rest.
  await page.click("#spawn1");
  await page.click("#spawn1");
  await expect(page.locator("#counts")).toHaveText(/3 nodes/, { timeout: 30_000 });

  await compileAndLaunch(page, SPINNER, "spinner");

  // The control plane notices the overdue attempt and offers a twin (tier three); the tab that is
  // stuck is killed at its own deadline and carries on. Either way the cluster is not wedged.
  await expect
    .poll(async () => page.evaluate(seenBy), { timeout: 120_000, intervals: [1_000] })
    .toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([expect.stringMatching(/taskSpeculated|taskReassigned/)]));
  // The instant task finished, so the stage was not blocked by the spinning one.
  const seen = await page.evaluate(seenBy);
  expect(seen).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["taskDone"]));
  // Every node is still there: a deadline kill terminates a sandbox worker, not a tab.
  await expect(page.locator("#counts")).toHaveText(/3 nodes/);
  await expect(page.locator("#mine .row").first()).toContainText(/idle|busy/, { timeout: 30_000 });
  // Leave the machine as we found it.
  await page.click("#killExecution");
  await expect(page.locator("#failure")).toContainText("cancelled by an operator", {
    timeout: 30_000,
  });
});
